# Remote Logger for Home Assistant

> Remote Logging for Home Assistant using Syslog or OTEL

Remote Logger is a Home Assistant custom integration (installed via the Home Assistant Marketplace) that forwards Home Assistant log records and selected events to a remote Syslog server or an OpenTelemetry (OTLP) collector, with structured multi-line entries and stack traces.


# Getting started

# Remote Logger for Home Assistant

Use log aggregation and analysis tools to get a complete picture of your home automation. Remote Logger for Home Assistant listens to Home Assistant logging at source and sends structured log events to a remote Syslog or OpenTelemetry (OTLP) collector. Optionally forwards other Home Assistant events, such as lifecycle events, service calls, configuration updates, state changes.

Unlike many logging solutions that scrape consoles logs, Remote Logger taps into either the root Python logger or the `system_log_event` Event fired by Home Assistant, preserving the **full structure so multi-line logs and stacktraces are preserved as single log entries**, utilizes the Home Assistant logic to **tie exceptions back to source code lines**, and will capture script names, line numbers and versions properly.

Only Home Assistant server itself, with its custom components is supported. Logs from *apps* (previously known as 'add-ins'), HAOS or the HA Supervisor aren't provided as events to be captured, so require an alternative solution, like Bert Baron's [LogSpout Home Assistant App](https://github.com/bertbaron/hassio-addons/tree/main/logspout) will cover these. It can be used in combination with *Remote Logger* so that Home Assistant has good structured logs, and everything else is at least logged. Since it uses Syslog and OTLP it can also be easily integrated with practically everything else in your environment, including SIEM cybersecurity logs from firewalls, Unifi networking, Docker logs etc. See the section on [aggregators](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/aggregators/) for suggestions if you're not familiar with these.

Translations are available for Dutch, English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese, Simplified Mandarin and Spanish.

## Installation

Install **Remote Logger** from the [Home Assistant Marketplace](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/marketplace): go to **Settings → Marketplace** and search for **Remote Logger**. Before Home Assistant 2026.11, install it from [HACS](https://www.hacs.xyz/docs/use/) instead.

The integration installs using the Home Assistant integrations page, and has **no YAML configuration**. Every setting is described in [Configuration](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/).

### Changing Settings

To change where logs are sent (host, port, TLS, token, headers and the other connection settings), open the entry on the integration's page and choose **Reconfigure**. The **Configure** button covers the log level and which Home Assistant events are forwarded.

### Event Based Logging

If choosing event based logging over the Python root logger, then a YAML change is required to the Home Assistant [System Log](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/system_log/) integration, to enable event forwarding for `system_log_event`. This is not required if using the default Python root logger approach.

Home Assistant Configuration

```yaml
system_log:
    fire_event: true
```

Choosing a Log Format

If you're not sure about which log format to choose, Open Telemetry (*aka* **OTEL Logging**, *aka* **OTLP**) is the best if you have a modern logging service that can handle it. It has the richest format, for example knows how to hold a multi-line stacktrace attached to a log message, and generally requires minimal configuration. Syslog is the best choice if the back end logging is more primitive, since it has been around since the dawn of time, although is much more semantically limited.

## Open Telemetry (OTEL)

Logs are sent using Open Telemetry Logs specification over a [Open Telemetry Protocol](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otlp/)(OTLP) connection, either as Protobuf or JSON, and currently only as HTTP (gRPC may be added in future).

For more information, see [OpenTelemetry Logging](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/).

Log records are collected and sent in a bundle

## Syslog

Messages are sent using the more recent [RFC5424](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5424) format, with additional structured data using OTEL taxonomy (see [Additional Attributes](#additional-attributes)).

Syslog can be sent as TCP or UDP.

**Strict RFC 5424 mode** is for receivers that check messages closely, such as Grafana Alloy. Turn it on in the Syslog setup form, or later with **Reconfigure**. Structured data then uses Home Assistant's own names, such as `name`, `source`, `exception` and `event_type`, and event data keys are shortened to fit the RFC's 32-character limit (for example `new_state.attributes.friendly_name` becomes `new.attr.friendly_name`). `MSGID` is cut to 32 characters, and the SD-ID is `homeassistant@<number>`, using the [IANA Private Enterprise Number](https://www.iana.org/assignments/enterprise-numbers/) you enter, or 67614, the Rhizomatics PEN, if you leave it empty. For testing, you can enter 32473, the RFC 5612 documentation number, instead. Without strict mode, the OTEL names below are used.

## Events

### System Log Event

Note the requirement at [Installation](#installation) to enable this event, which isn't fired by default. This is limited to *Warning* and *Error* events. Find out more at the [System Log](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/system_log/) integration documentation.

*Remote Logger* will omit its own log events from the stream, to prevent the possibility of event loops. As an alternative, error stats and messages are available as diagnostic entities.

#### Additional Attributes

The following additional attributes, derived directly from the Home Assistant log event, are provided as Syslog `STRUCTURED-DATA` attributes, or OTEL attributes.

- `code.file.path`
- `code.line.number`
- `code.function.name` (this is the `logger` value from Home Assistant)
- `exception.count`
- `exception.first_occurred`
- `exception.stacktrace`

OTEL taxonomy is used for both OTEL and Syslog since there's no standard taxonomy at this level of Syslog.

### Other Events

*Remote Logger* can log any Home Assistant event, and knows about the core ones, in order to create a more readable message. Find out more in the [Events](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/events/) guidance.

## Log Servers

There are a zillion possible solutions for capturing, analyzing, aggregating and storing logs. Generally a log setup requires:

- **Collector** - The thing that sits on the monitored service and sends out the logs. This *Remote Logger* is a collector for Home Assistant core, as is [LogSpout Home Assistant App](https://github.com/bertbaron/hassio-addons/tree/main/logspout) for HAOS.
- **Aggregator** - Receives logs from collectors, enriches, filters, converts formats and forwards on. See [Log Aggregators](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/aggregators/) for more information.
- **Store** - Typically a database that holds the logs, and any column indexes or free text search indexes
- **Analytics** - Query by SQL or similar, keyword search, graphing, counting etc

These suggestions are for options that are open source and free, at least for home use, and will work in Docker.

- [Vector](https://vector.dev) as the aggregator and [GreptimeDb](https://greptime.com) as the store and analytics - they are fast, lightweight, open source, customizable and run under Docker. Vector has support for OTEL logging, as well as Syslog, and has good remapping ability to fine tune each source. Its then easy to pull in logs from Docker servers, firewalls, Unifi switches or wherever else into one time-line, as well as server and network metrics. See the [examples](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/examples/vector_greptimedb/) for a sample configuration.
- [OpenObserve](https://openobserve.ai) can do all three jobs ( aggregator, store, analytics ) for many sources, although it now recommends using Vector for Syslog. It also has a more functional log query interface, especially for people used to Splunk, and reuses the *VRL* (Vector Remap Language) for its own pipelines.

## Diagnostic Entities

Home Assistant sensors are created and updated to monitor log activity, plus any errors either generating log messages or posting them to remote servers. The **Log Events** and **Postings** counters change on most updates, so they are disabled by default; enable them on the Remote Logger device if you want them.

If logs don't arrive, see [Troubleshooting](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/troubleshooting/), which also lists the known limitations.

## Diagnostic Actions

Home Assistant actions are supported to send a test event, force flush the log buffers and show the last payload posted.

## Removal

1. In Home Assistant, go to **Settings** > **Devices & services** > **Remote Logger**. For each entry, open its menu (⋮) and choose **Delete**. Log export stops straight away, and the diagnostic sensors and their device are removed.
1. To remove the integration's files as well, go to **Settings → Marketplace**, open **Remote Logger** and choose **Uninstall** from the three dots menu. (**Delete and uninstall** there does step 1 as well.) Before Home Assistant 2026.11, open **HACS**, find **Remote Logger**, choose **Remove**, then restart Home Assistant.
1. If you added `fire_event: true` under `system_log:` in `configuration.yaml` only for Remote Logger, you can take it out again.

## Rhizomatics Open Source for Home Assistant

### Home Assistant Marketplace

- [Appliance AutoNotify](https://appliance-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) - Live activities on your phone for dishwashers, robot vacuums, power monitors etc with no config, no YAML, no blueprints, no automations.

- [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) - Instant notifications for Frigate (and other camera systems coming) with no config, no blueprints, no YAML, no automations.
- [Supernotify](https://supernotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) - Unified notification for easy multi-channel messaging, including powerful chime and security camera integration.

### Python / Docker

- [Anpr2MQTT](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk) - Integrate with ANPR/ALPR licence plate cameras via file system (NAS/FTP) to MQTT with optional image analysis and UK DVLA integration.
- [Home Assistant REPL](https://homeassistant-repl.rhizomatics.org.uk) - Python REPL for direct internal API and SQL access for Home Assistant development and data exploration.
- [Updates2MQTT](https://updates2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk) - Automatically notify via MQTT on Docker image updates, with advanced handling to extract versions and release notes from images, and option to remotely pull and restart containers from Home Assistant. Also available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/updates2mqtt/)

# Configuration

Remote Logger is set up from **Settings** > **Devices & services** > **Add integration**. There is no YAML configuration. The settings come in two groups:

- **Connection settings** say where logs go. They are asked for when the entry is added, and changed later with **Reconfigure** on the entry's menu. A test log record is sent to check them before they are saved.
- **Event settings** say what is sent. They are asked for after the connection settings, and changed later with **Configure**.

## OpenTelemetry (OTLP) Connection

Logs are posted over HTTP to `http(s)://<host>:<port><path>`.

| Setting                    | Default    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Collector host             | (required) | Hostname or IP address of the OTLP collector.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Collector port             | `4318`     | HTTP port of the collector. gRPC (port 4317) isn't supported.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Use TLS (HTTPS)            | off        | Send over HTTPS. The collector's certificate is checked.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Payload encoding           | `protobuf` | `protobuf` or `json`. Both are standard OTLP; use `json` if your collector only accepts that.                                                                                                                                                      |
| Batch max size             | `20`       | Records held before an early send, from 1 to 10000. See [Sending Logs](#sending-logs).                                                                                                                                                             |
| Custom resource attributes | (none)     | Comma-separated `key=value` pairs added to the resource of every record, for example `deployment.environment=production,service.namespace=home`.                                                                                                   |
| Token type                 | `bearer`   | How the token is put in the `Authorization` header: `bearer` sends `Bearer <token>`; `basic` base64-encodes a `username:password` token; `raw_basic` sends `Basic <token>` with a token that is already encoded; `api_key` sends `ApiKey <token>`. |
| Access token               | (none)     | Optional token for the `Authorization` header. Use TLS when sending a token, or a repair issue is raised.                                                                                                                                          |
| Additional headers         | (none)     | Extra HTTP headers, one `Name: value` per entry, for example `stream-name: my-stream`.                                                                                                                                                             |
| Logs endpoint path         | `/v1/logs` | Path after `host:port`. Some services add a prefix, such as `/api/otlp/v1/logs`.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Client timeout             | `10`       | Seconds to wait for the collector, from 1 to 300.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

If the collector answers HTTP 401 or 403, Home Assistant asks for a new token (re-authentication) and shows the entry as needing attention.

## Syslog Connection

Messages use [RFC 5424](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5424) format. Only one Syslog entry can be added.

| Setting                 | Default         | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Syslog server host      | (required)      | Hostname or IP address of the syslog server.                                                                                                           |
| Syslog server port      | `514`           | Port of the syslog server.                                                                                                                             |
| Transport protocol      | `udp`           | `udp` sends and forgets; `tcp` keeps a connection and uses octet-counted framing (RFC 6587).                                                           |
| Use TLS (TCP only)      | off             | Encrypt the TCP connection. Not available with UDP.                                                                                                    |
| CA certificate file     | (none)          | Path to a PEM file with the certificate authority for a private CA. Leave empty to use the system certificate store.                                   |
| Client certificate file | (none)          | Path to a PEM client certificate, for servers that require mutual TLS.                                                                                 |
| Client key file         | (none)          | Path to the PEM private key for the client certificate, if it isn't in the same file.                                                                  |
| Application name        | `homeassistant` | The `APP-NAME` field of each message.                                                                                                                  |
| Syslog facility         | `local0`        | Facility used to work out the `PRI` value.                                                                                                             |
| Batch max size          | `20`            | Messages held before an early send, from 1 to 10000. See [Sending Logs](#sending-logs).                                                                |
| Client timeout          | `10`            | Seconds to wait when connecting over TCP, from 1 to 300.                                                                                               |
| Strict RFC 5424 mode    | off             | Syslog-native output for receivers that check messages closely, such as Grafana Alloy. See [Syslog](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/#syslog). |
| Enterprise number       | `67614`         | IANA Private Enterprise Number for the strict mode SD-ID `homeassistant@<number>`. 32473 (RFC 5612) can be used for testing.                           |

## Event Settings

These are the same for both backends.

| Setting                                              | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use System Log events in place of Python root logger | off     | Off: records are taken from Python's root logger, at or above the minimum log level. On: records come from the `system_log_event` event, which only carries warnings and errors, and needs `fire_event: true` under `system_log:` (see [Event Based Logging](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/#event-based-logging)). |
| Minimum log level                                    | `INFO`  | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR` or `CRITICAL`. Only used with the root logger.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Home Assistant lifecycle events                      | off     | Start, started and stop events.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Home Assistant core change events                    | off     | Components loaded, configuration and service changes, dashboards, themes and users.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Home Assistant core activity                         | off     | Service calls, automations triggered and scripts started.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| State changes, without attributes or context         | off     | Each state change with its old and new state only, and logbook entries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| State changes                                        | off     | Each state change in full, and logbook entries. Choose only one of the two state change options.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Serialize event data into log body                   | off     | Puts the event data in the log body as JSON, keeping only `entity_id`, `domain` and `service` as attributes. Off, each data field is its own attribute, so a log database may make a column for every field.                                                                                                                  |
| Custom events                                        | (none)  | Other Home Assistant event names to send, one per entry, for example `zha_event`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Suppress system_log_event as event name              | on      | Records from the system log are sent without an event name. Turn off when using Remote Logger as a general event recorder, so all event types can be told apart.                                                                                                                                                              |

See [Events](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/events/index.md) for what each event group contains.

## Sending Logs

Records are buffered in memory and sent in batches:

- every 120 seconds;
- sooner, when the buffer reaches the **Batch max size**;
- when Home Assistant stops, or the entry is unloaded or reconfigured;
- when the `remote_logger.flush` action is called.

If an OTLP collector can't be reached, or rejects a batch, that batch is dropped and counted by the **Posting Errors** sensor. Syslog messages that couldn't be sent are kept and retried on the next send. At most 10000 records are buffered; beyond that the oldest are dropped. A warning is logged once when the collector becomes unavailable, and an info message once when it can be reached again.

The diagnostic sensors are read from in-memory counters every 30 seconds.
# Guides

# Event Logging

The core job of Remote Logger is listening to either the root system logger (Python `logging`) or subscribe to the `system_log_events` raised by Home Assistant, and forwarding on as Syslog or OTLP messages. The resulting message is the same whatever mechanism is used, the main difference is the Root Logger approach allows `INFO` or `DEBUG` logs.

However, it can also be useful to listen and log many of the other [events](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/events/) that Home Assistant emits.

## Home Assistant Events

- [Platform Lifecycle Events](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/events/#homeassistant_stop-homeassistant_final_write-homeassistant_close) such as `homeassistant_stop`
- [Component Lifecycle Events](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/events/#component_loaded)
- Registry Events - for new and changed devices, services, entities, users, labels, floors, areas and categories
- [Service Calls](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/events/#call_service)
- [State Changes](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/events/#state_changed) - state value often with a slew of additional attributes
- [Automation Executions](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/events/#automation_triggered) - for automations, scripts and scenes
- Custom Component events - like `autoarm_change`

## Selecting Events in Remote Logger

The screen below is shown as a second config page once you submit the main configure logging hub configuration.

The free-form event box can be used as an alternative to pick specific Home Assistant events, or any other custom component events. Its easy to log whole categories of these from the Remote Logger configuration, or select individual ones you need. State changes can be huge in volume, and can also stress log aggregators by creating huge numbers of columns, so Remote Logger offers two versions of state logging - the bare state, or the full version with attributes ( and also a choice in how events are sent over JSON, as simplified messages, or full raw native ones with all the fields).

| Bundle             | Description                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Lifecycle          | Home Assistant server start and stop events                                                                         |
| Core Changes       | Components and services loading or unloading, config reapplied                                                      |
| Core Activity      | Actions, mobile actions, scripts, automations executed                                                              |
| State Changes      | Entity state changes and log book entries, with states stripped of attributes and context to avoid huge log entries |
| Full State Changes | Entity state changes and log book entries, full and untrimmed                                                       |

State Changes and Full State Changes are mutually exclusive - only one may be enabled at a time, since the full version is a superset of the bare one. Enabling both together is rejected with a validation error, and the form will show your other inputs unchanged so you can correct it.

## Beyond Home Assistant

Debugging issues is much easier with full context, not only from Home Assistant itself, also add-on Apps running in HAOS, and other services on the network. For example, include logging from Frigate via a Docker syslog or OTLP collector, or network issues from a Unifi or OPNSense installation.

OpenObserve, GreptimeDB and similar tools (there's a [big list of OTEL vendors and projects](https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/vendors/)) can also pull in metrics and traces, for a fuller picture, though its also easy to get overwhelmed - CPU, storage, mentally - by the sheer scale of what could be aggregated, even in a home lab.

See the [examples](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/examples/index.md) for working configuration.

# Log Aggregators

There are many aggregators that will accept Syslog and OTLP (Otel Logging), some of which are open source, free for self-hosting and work well.

Some aggregators can directly consume remote logs, while others need an ingestion/transformation engine like Datadog's [Vector](https://vector.dev), [FluentD](https://www.fluentd.org) etc. These also allow logs to be pulled in, so events in HomeAssistant can be seen in the context of what's happening in HAOS Apps, docker containers, network switches, firewalls etc.

## OpenObserve

Tip

One quick way to get this is to use [OpenObserve app for Home Assistant](https://github.com/Sm0by/ha-addon-openobserve), installed as a custom repo through *Settings* | *Apps*, accessed and backed up via Home Assistant.

This is one of the easiest to use, since it can accept OTLP natively so doesn't need any other components, though it can work with Vector and others, and now needs Vector for Syslog. It also has a Splunk type UI to show the schema and automatically populate known values for each field to make quick filtering easier.

To configure the preferred OTLP logging, a few overrides are needed.

Use the built-in configuration generator in OpenObserve, as below:

OpenObserve has a non-default port, a non-default API end-point and needs additional headers.

*Remote Logger* has options to support all of these, as in this example:

Note that *Raw Basic* has been selected rather than *Basic* since the token provided by OpenObserve has already been encoded.

## GreptimeDB

Uses Vector for ingestion, and no transforms are needed when using OTLP.

```yaml
sources:
  otlp:
    type: opentelemetry
    http:
      address: 0.0.0.0:4318
    use_otlp_decoding: false
sinks:
  greptime:
    inputs:
      - "otlp.logs"
    type: "greptimedb_logs"
    endpoint: http://greptime:4000
    dbname: public
    compression: gzip
    table: logs
```

# Security

Remote Logger copies logs and events out of Home Assistant to another system. That system, and the network in between, then hold whatever was in them, so it is worth choosing what is sent and how.

To report a vulnerability, see the [security policy](https://github.com/rhizomatics/remote_logger/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## What is exported

| Setting                                      | What leaves Home Assistant                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Always                                       | Log records at the chosen level and above: logger name, source file and line, message and stack trace |
| Lifecycle events                             | Start and stop events, with no personal data                                                          |
| Core change events                           | Registry changes, including user ids for added, changed and removed users                             |
| Core activity                                | Every action call with its data, automation and script runs, notification actions from the mobile app |
| State changes, without attributes or context | Entity id, old and new state for every state change                                                   |
| State changes                                | The same, plus every attribute and the context, including the id of the user who caused it            |
| Custom events                                | All the data of each event named                                                                      |

Action calls and state attributes can hold things you would not want in a log database: location and presence, who is at home, the text of notifications, and what is playing or being watched. Switch on only what you will use.

### Redaction

The values of event data and state attributes with these names are replaced with `**REDACTED**` before export, at any depth:

`access_token`, `api_key`, `client_secret`, `code`, `entity_picture`, `password`, `pin`, `refresh_token`, `secret`, `token`

This keeps alarm and lock codes, and the access tokens of cameras and media players, in Home Assistant. It goes by the name only, so a secret under a different name, or written into a log message or a state, is still exported.

## Protecting logs in transit

| Protocol                 | Encryption | Notes                                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| OTLP with TLS (HTTPS)    | Yes        | The collector's certificate is verified                                                        |
| OTLP without TLS         | No         | The token and all logs are readable on the network. A repair issue is raised if a token is set |
| Syslog over TCP with TLS | Yes        | The server's certificate is verified                                                           |
| Syslog over TCP          | No         |                                                                                                |
| Syslog over UDP          | No         | Can't be encrypted, and messages can be lost or forged by others on the network                |

Plain HTTP or Syslog is reasonable when the collector is on the same host as Home Assistant, or on a network you trust. Otherwise use TLS.

### Private certificates and mutual TLS for Syslog

For a Syslog server with a certificate from your own certificate authority, give the path to the CA certificate, as a PEM file Home Assistant can read, for example `/ssl/syslog-ca.pem`. If the server requires client certificates (mutual TLS), also give the client certificate and, if it is in a separate file, its key. Requiring client certificates is the one way a Syslog server can be sure a record came from Home Assistant.

## Actions

| Action                   | Who can call it                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `remote_logger.send_log` | Any user, automation or script. A record sent by a user has that user's id added as `user.id` |
| `remote_logger.flush`    | Administrators, automations and scripts                                                       |
| `remote_logger.last_log` | Administrators, automations and scripts. Header values are masked in the result               |

An automation, or a script it starts, runs without a user and so is always allowed. A script started from a dashboard by a user who is not an administrator runs as that user, and can't call `flush` or `last_log`.

## The collector

Whatever receives the logs should itself need a login, and should not be reachable from the internet. The [examples](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/examples/index.md) are starting points for a home network, not hardened deployments: set your own passwords, pin image versions, and publish only the ports you use.

# Troubleshooting

## Known Limitations

- **Home Assistant core only.** Logs from apps (add-ons), the Supervisor and the operating system aren't sent. Use something like the [LogSpout Home Assistant App](https://github.com/bertbaron/hassio-addons/tree/main/logspout) alongside Remote Logger for those.
- **Records from before setup are missed.** Remote Logger starts listening when its entry is set up, so anything logged earlier in Home Assistant's startup isn't sent.
- **Remote Logger's own log records aren't sent**, to avoid loops. Its activity is shown by the diagnostic sensors.
- **System log events carry only warnings and errors.** With *Use System Log events in place of Python root logger* on, info and debug records aren't available.
- **OTLP over HTTP only.** gRPC isn't supported.
- **One Syslog entry.** Several OTLP entries can be added, one per collector host and port.
- **TLS for Syslog needs TCP.** Syslog over UDP is always unencrypted.
- **Delivery is best effort.** An OTLP batch that fails to send is dropped, Syslog over UDP has no acknowledgement, and at most 10000 records are held while the endpoint is unavailable. See [Sending Logs](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/#sending-logs).

## Setup Says It Can't Connect

When the connection settings are saved, a test log record is sent with the message *Home Assistant remote_logger configuration validation, safe to ignore*.

- Check the host and port, and that nothing between Home Assistant and the collector blocks the port.
- For OTLP, check **Use TLS** matches the collector (`http` or `https`), and the **Logs endpoint path**; many services want a prefix before `/v1/logs`.
- For Syslog with TLS, check the certificate file paths can be read by Home Assistant and are PEM files.

If the collector is down when Home Assistant starts, the entry shows as *retrying setup* and connects when the collector is back.

## No Logs Arrive

1. Wait up to two minutes: records are sent in batches. Calling the **Flush** action (`remote_logger.flush`) sends them straight away.
1. Look at the **Posting Errors** sensor on the Remote Logger device. Its `last_error_message` attribute has the collector's reply or the connection error.
1. Enable the **Postings** sensor (it's disabled by default) to see whether batches are being sent at all.
1. Call the **Last Log** action (`remote_logger.last_log`) to see the last payload that was sent.
1. With *Use System Log events in place of Python root logger* on, check `fire_event: true` is set under `system_log:` (see [Event Based Logging](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/#event-based-logging)).

The Home Assistant log shows one warning when the endpoint becomes unavailable, and one info message when it can be reached again.

## The Collector Rejects Records

- An OTLP collector that answers HTTP 4xx may not accept the **Payload encoding**; try `json` instead of `protobuf`, or the other way round.
- A Syslog receiver that drops or rejects messages, such as Grafana Alloy, may need **Strict RFC 5424 mode**.

## Repairs and Re-authentication

- **Access token sent without encryption**: an OTLP token is set but TLS is off. Reconfigure the entry to use TLS, or ignore the repair if the collector is on the same host or a trusted network.
- **Re-authentication**: the collector answered HTTP 401 or 403. Enter a new token in the prompt shown on the integration's page.

## Reporting a Problem

Download the diagnostics from the entry's menu (⋮ > **Download diagnostics**) and attach them to an [issue](https://github.com/rhizomatics/remote_logger/issues). Tokens, headers and the client key path are redacted, but the last payload sent is included, so check it for anything you don't want to share.
# Examples

# Example Configuration - OpenObserve with Vector

These are working examples, not ideal recommendations.

They are meant for a home network you trust: the syslog and OTLP listeners accept logs from anything that can reach them, without a login or encryption. Before using them, set your own passwords, pin the image versions rather than `latest`, and don't publish the ports beyond your own network. Vector is given the Docker socket, read-only, to collect container logs: that still lets it see everything about every container on the host.

The Vector config will also pull in Docker logs and systemd journal from the box on which it runs ( excluding Vector and OpenObserve from the Docker logging to prevent cycles).

OpenObserve handles OTLP directly, so Vector can be skipped if there's no syslog to capture, and no Docker ( or a native OTLP collector installed for Docker)

```yaml
 services:

  openobserve:
    image: public.ecr.aws/zinclabs/openobserve-enterprise:latest
    container_name: openobserve
    restart: always
    user: "994:994"
    environment:
      ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL: "REDACTED_OO_USER"
      ZO_ROOT_USER_PASSWORD: "REDACTED_OO_PASSWORD"
      ZO_DATA_DIR: "/data"
      ZO_ALLOW_USER_DEFINED_SCHEMAS: true
      ZO_SMTP_ENABLED: true
      ZO_SMTP_HOST: 10.111.10.100
      RUST_LOG: warn
      O2_AI_ENABLED: true
      O2_TOOL_API_URL: http://localhost:5080
      O2_MCP_VALIDATION_ENABLED: false
      O2_INCIDENTS_ENABLED: "true"
      O2_INCIDENTS_RCA_ENABLED: "true"
      O2_INCIDENTS_ALERT_GRAPH_ENABLED: "true"
    ports:
    - protocol: tcp
      published: 5080
      target: 5080
    volumes:
      - ./oo_data:/data
  vector:
    image: timberio/vector:latest-debian
    container_name: vector
    user: "994:994"
    group_add:
      - "119"
      - "101"
    command: --config /etc/vector/vector.yaml
    volumes:
      - ./conf:/etc/vector
      - ./logs:/logs
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - ./vector_data:/var/vector
    environment:
      VECTOR_LOG: warn
    ports:
      - 127.0.0.1:8686:8686 # Vector API, from this host only
      - 514:514/udp
      - 5514:5514/tcp
    cap_add:
      - CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
    restart: always

  o2-sre-agent:
    # The AI add-on, completely usable without this
    image: public.ecr.aws/zinclabs/o2-sre-agent:latest
    container_name: o2-sre-agent
    restart: always
    environment:
      O2_SRE_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      O2_SRE_PORT: 5088
      O2_SRE_LOG_LEVEL: INFO
      O2_OTEL_ENABLED: true
      O2_AI_PROVIDER: anthropic
      O2_AI_API_KEY: REDACTED_CLAUDE_API_KEY
      O2_TOOL_API_URL: http://openobserve:5080/api/default/mcp
      O2_MCP_VALIDATION_ENABLED: "true"
      O2_MCP_VALIDATION_RETRY: "true"
      O2_MCP_CONTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED: "true"
      O2_MCP_CONTENT_VALIDATION_MODE: "hybrid"
      O2_MCP_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED: "true"
      O2_MCP_USERNAME: "REDACTED_MCP_USER"
      O2_MCP_PASSWORD: "REDACTED_MCP_PASSWORD"

    ports:
      - protocol: tcp
        published: 5088
        target: 5088
```

```text
parsed, err = parse_json(.message)
if err == null {
  .severity_text = "UNSPECIFIED"
  .severity_number = 0

  level = downcase(string(parsed.level) ?? "")
  if level == "trace" {
    .severity_text = "TRACE"
    .severity_number = 1
  } else if level == "debug" {
    .severity_text = "DEBUG"
    .severity_number = 5
  } else if level == "info" {
    .severity_text = "INFO"
    .severity_number = 9
  } else if level == "warn" || level == "warning" {
    .severity_text = "WARN"
    .severity_number = 13
  } else if level == "error" {
    .severity_text = "ERROR"
    .severity_number = 17
  } else if level == "fatal" || level == "panic" {
    .severity_text = "FATAL"
    .severity_number = 21
  }
}

resourceLogs,err = [{
        "resource": {
        "attributes": [
                  { "key": "source_type", "value": { "stringValue": .source_type  } },
                  { "key": "service.name", "value": { "stringValue": .container_name} },
                  { "key": "net.host.ip", "value": { "stringValue": .source_ip } },
                  { "key": "host.hostname", "value": { "stringValue": .host } }
        ]
       },
       "scopeLogs": [{
                     "scope": {
                     "name": .msgid
                    },
                     "logRecords": [{
                       "timeUnixNano": to_unix_timestamp!(.timestamp, unit: "nanoseconds"),
                       "body": { "stringValue": .message },
                       "severityText": .severity_text,
                       "severityNumber": .severity_number,
                       "attributes": [
                              { "key": "syslog.procid", "value": { "stringValue": to_string(.procid) } },
                              { "key": "syslog.facility", "value": { "stringValue": .facility } },
                              { "key": "syslog.version", "value": { "stringValue": to_string(.version) } },
                              { "key": "docker.container.id", "value": { "stringValue": to_string(.container_id) } },
                              { "key": "docker.image", "value": { "stringValue": .image } },
                              { "key": "docker.stream", "value": { "stringValue": to_string(.stream) } },
                              { "key": "docker.container.created", "value": { "stringValue": to_string(.container_created_at) } }
                             ]
                       }]
                   }]
      }]
      del(.message)
      del(.timestamp)
      del(.service)
      del(.source_type)
      del(.appname)
      del(.facility)
      del(.host)
      del(.hostname)
      del(.severity)
      del(.source_ip)
      del(.severity_number)
      del(.severity_text)
      assert!(err == null,message:err)
      .resourceLogs = resourceLogs
```

# remove Home Assistant from HAOS LogSpout since richer events received from Remote Logger

```yaml
data_dir: /var/vector
schema:
  log_namespace: false

api:
    enabled: true
    address: 0.0.0.0:8686

sources:
  vector_logs:
   type: "internal_logs"

  dockernuc_docker:
    type: docker_logs
    exclude_containers:
      - vector
      - greptime
      - openobserve

  syslog_daemon:
    type: syslog
    address: 0.0.0.0:514
    mode: udp

  syslog_daemon_tcp:
     type: syslog
     address: 0.0.0.0:5514
     mode: tcp

transforms:
  vector_errors:
    type: "filter"
    inputs:
      - "vector_logs"
    condition: '.metadata.level != "INFO"'

  docker_to_otlp:
    type: remap
    inputs:
      - dockernuc_docker
    file: /etc/vector/docker_to_otlp.vrl

  syslog_to_otlp:
    type: remap
    inputs:
       - syslog_daemon
       - syslog_daemon_tcp
    drop_on_abort: true
    drop_on_error: true
    reroute_dropped: true
    file: /etc/vector/syslog_to_otlp.vrl


sinks:
  file_vector:
    type: "file"
    inputs:
      - "vector_errors"
    compression: "none"
    path: "/logs/internal_vector_errors.log"
    encoding:
      codec: "json"
  file_dropped:
    type: "file"
    inputs:
      - "syslog_to_otlp.dropped"
    path: "/logs/syslog_remap_drops.log"
    compression: "none"
    encoding:
      codec: "json"
  openobserve:
    inputs:
      - syslog_to_otlp
      - docker_to_otlp
    type: opentelemetry
    protocol:
      type: http
      uri: "http://openobserve:5080/api/default/v1/logs"
      encoding:
        codec: otlp
      method: post
      request:
        headers:
          stream-name: default
      auth:
        strategy: basic
        user: "REDACTED_OO_USER"
        password: "REDACTED_OO_PASSWORD"
    healthcheck:
      enabled: true
      uri: http://openobserve:5080/healthz
```

# Example Configuration - GreptimeDb with Vector

These are working examples, not ideal recommendations.

They are meant for a home network you trust: the syslog and OTLP listeners accept logs from anything that can reach them, without a login or encryption. Before using them, set your own passwords, pin the image versions rather than `latest`, and don't publish the ports beyond your own network. Vector is given the Docker socket, read-only, to collect container logs: that still lets it see everything about every container on the host.

The Vector config will also pull in Docker logs and systemd journal from the box on which it runs ( excluding Vector and Greptime from the Docker logging to prevent cycles).

```yaml
services:
  vector:
    image: timberio/vector:latest-debian
    container_name: vector
    user: "994:994"
    group_add:
      - "119" # docker group, for access to daemon socket
      - "101" # systemd-journal group
    command: --config /etc/vector/vector.yaml
    volumes:
      - ./conf:/etc/vector
      - ./logs:/logs
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - ./vector_data:/var/vector
    ports:
      - 127.0.0.1:8686:8686 # Vector API, from this host only
      - 514:514/udp
      - 5514:5514/tcp
      - 4317:4317/tcp # otel gRPC
      - 4318:4318/tcp # otel http
    #environment:
        #- VECTOR_LOG=debug,hyper=debug,h2=debug
    cap_add:
      - CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
    restart: always
  greptime:
    image: greptime/greptimedb:latest
    container_name: greptime
    restart: always
    volumes:
      - ./greptimedb_data:/greptimedb_data
      - ./conf/greptime.toml:/etc/greptime/config.toml
    ports:
      - 4000:4000
      - 4001:4001
      - 4002:4002
      - 4003:4003
    command:
      - standalone
      - start
      - --http-addr=0.0.0.0:4000
      - --rpc-bind-addr=0.0.0.0:4001
      - --mysql-addr=127.0.0.1:4002
      - --postgres-addr=127.0.0.1:4003
      - --config-file=/etc/greptime/config.toml
```

```toml
## The default timezone of the server.
default_timezone = "Europe/London"

## The default column prefix for auto-created time index and value columns.
default_column_prefix = "greptime"

## Initialize all regions in the background during the startup.
## By default, it provides services after all regions have been initialized.
init_regions_in_background = false

## Parallelism of initializing regions.
init_regions_parallelism = 16

## The maximum current queries allowed to be executed. Zero means unlimited.
## NOTE: This setting affects scan_memory_limit's privileged tier allocation.
## When set, 70% of queries get privileged memory access (full scan_memory_limit).
## The remaining 30% get standard tier access (70% of scan_memory_limit).
max_concurrent_queries = 3

## Enable telemetry to collect anonymous usage data. Enabled by default.
enable_telemetry = false

[http]
addr = "0.0.0.0:4000"
## HTTP request timeout. Set to 0 to disable timeout.
timeout = "0s"
## HTTP request body limit.
## The following units are supported: `B`, `KB`, `KiB`, `MB`, `MiB`, `GB`, `GiB`, `TB`, `TiB`, `PB`, `PiB`.
## Set to 0 to disable limit.
body_limit = "64MB"
enable_cors = true
prom_validation_mode = "lossy"

[mysql]
enable = true
addr = "127.0.0.1:4002"
## The number of server worker threads.
runtime_size = 2
## Server-side keep-alive time.
## Set to 0 (default) to disable.

## Maximum entries in the MySQL prepared statement cache; default is 10,000.
prepared_stmt_cache_size= 10000
# MySQL server TLS options.

enable = true
addr = "127.0.0.1:4003"
## The number of server worker threads.
runtime_size = 2
## Server-side keep-alive time.
## Set to 0 (default) to disable.
keep_alive = "0s"

[opentsdb]
enable = true

[influxdb]
enable = true

[jaeger]
enable = false

[prom_store]
enable = true
## Whether to store the data from Prometheus remote write in metric engine.
with_metric_engine = true

[wal]
provider = "raft_engine"
dir = "./greptimedb_data/wal"
file_size = "128MB"

[procedure]

## Memory pool size for query execution operators (aggregation, sorting, join).
## Supports absolute size (e.g., "2GB", "4GB") or percentage of system memory (e.g., "20%").
## Setting it to 0 disables the limit (unbounded, default behavior).
## When this limit is reached, queries will fail with ResourceExhausted error.
## NOTE: This does NOT limit memory used by table scans.
memory_pool_size = "25%"

[storage]

type = "File"
cache_capacity = "5GiB"

[logging]
dir = "/logs"
level = "info"
enable_otlp_tracing = false
append_stdout = true
log_format = "json"
max_log_files = 720

[slow_query]
enable = true
```

```yaml
data_dir: /var/vector
schema:
  log_namespace: false

api:
    enabled: true
    address: 0.0.0.0:8686

sources:

  vector_logs:
    type: "internal_logs"

  otlp:
    type: opentelemetry
    grpc:
      address: 0.0.0.0:4317
    http:
      address: 0.0.0.0:4318
      headers: []
      keepalive:
        max_connection_age_jitter_factor: 0.1
        max_connection_age_secs: 300
    use_otlp_decoding: false

  dockernuc_journald:
    type: journald

  dockernuc_docker:
    type: docker_logs
    exclude_containers:
      - vector
      - greptime

  syslog_daemon:
    type: syslog
    address: 0.0.0.0:514
    mode: udp

  syslog_daemon_tcp:
     type: syslog
     address: 0.0.0.0:5514
     mode: tcp

transforms:
  vector_errors:
    type: "filter"
    inputs:
      - "vector_logs"
    condition: '.metadata.level != "INFO"'

  remap_docker:
    inputs:
      - "dockernuc_docker"
    type: "remap"
    source: |
      # Map container_name to appname
      if exists(.container_name) {
        .appname = .container_name
        del(.container_name)
      }
      . = filter(object(.)) -> |key, _value| {
        !starts_with(key, "label")
      }

  remap_syslog:
    inputs:
       - "syslog_daemon"
       - "syslog_daemon_tcp"
    type:   "remap"
    drop_on_error: false
    drop_on_abort: true
    source: |
      # Ensure message is a string and strip ANSI color codes
      .message = strip_ansi_escape_codes(string!(.message))

      # Try to parse syslog format
      parsed, err = parse_syslog(.message)

      # remove Home Assistant from HAOS LogSpout since richer events received from Remote Logger
      if .appname == "homeassistant" {
        abort
      }

      if err == null {
        . = merge(., parsed)
        # Normalize msg -> message
        if exists(.msg) {
          .message = .msg
          del(.msg)
        }
      }

      # Ensure consistent types matching schema
      .procid = if exists(.procid) {
        if is_string(.procid) {
          to_int(.procid) ?? 0
        } else if is_integer(.procid) {
        .procid
        } else {
        0
      }
      } else {
        0
      }
      # remove redundant timestamp in message
      ts_match = parse_regex(.message, r'^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d+Z?\s*(?P<msg>.*)') ?? {}
      if exists(ts_match.msg) {
        .message = string!(ts_match.msg)
      }
      .severity = if exists(.severity) { string!(.severity) } else { "info" }

      # CRITICAL: Remove timestamp string - conflicts with greptime_timestamp
      del(.timestamp)
      del(.version)  # Also remove version if not needed

sinks:
  file_vector:
    type: "file"
    inputs:
      - "vector_errors"
    compression: "none"
    path: "/logs/internal_vector.log"
    encoding:
      codec: "json"
  greptime:
    inputs:
      - "remap_syslog"
      - "remap_docker"
      - "otlp.logs"
      - "dockernuc_journald"
    type: "greptimedb_logs"
    endpoint: http://greptime:4000
    dbname: public
    compression: gzip
    table: logs
```
# Optional

# 2.13.0

Remote Logger now meets Platinum, the highest level of the Home Assistant [Integration Quality Scale](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/quality_scale/) (self-assessed). See [quality_scale.yaml](https://github.com/rhizomatics/remote_logger/blob/main/custom_components/remote_logger/quality_scale.yaml) for how each rule is met.

## ✨ Enhancements

- Diagnostics can be downloaded from the entry's menu, with the token, headers and client key path redacted
- When the collector can't be reached, one warning is logged, and one info message when it is back, instead of a warning on every send
- The **Log Events** and **Postings** sensors are disabled by default for new entries, since they change on most updates. Existing entries keep their sensors as they are
- Icons for the diagnostic sensors and the actions
- New [Configuration](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/) page describing every setting with its default, and how logs are batched and sent
- New [Troubleshooting](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/troubleshooting/) page, including the known limitations
- The translated READMEs have the same additions as the English one

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Syslog messages that failed to send were counted as successful postings, so the **Posting Errors** sensor never showed Syslog failures
- The setup and reconfigure forms gave the default batch size as 100 (it is 20) and the default Syslog facility as `user` (it is `local0`)
- The client timeout field had no label or description on any connection form, nor the batch size field on the Syslog forms

## 📝 Other changes

### Internal

- Minimum test coverage raised from 90% to 95%
- The sensor platform declares `PARALLEL_UPDATES = 0`, since its updates only read counters in memory

# 2.12.0

A security review of the integration and of how it is built and released. See the new [Security](https://remote-logger.rhizomatics.org.uk/security/) page for what is exported and how to protect it.

## 🚨 Breaking changes

- The `last_log` and `flush` actions are now for administrators only. Automations, and scripts they start, are not affected
- `last_log` gives back log content, which Home Assistant otherwise shows only to administrators
- Values of event data and state attributes named `code`, `pin`, `password`, `secret`, `token`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `api_key`, `client_secret` or `entity_picture` are now exported as `**REDACTED**`
- Alarm and lock codes in action calls, and camera access tokens in state changes, were previously sent to the collector
- Syslog with TLS selected and UDP as the protocol is now refused in the configuration, since UDP was sent unencrypted regardless
- Existing entries set up this way carry on as before, with a warning in the log
- Syslog `APP-NAME`, `MSGID` and structured data names now have spaces, and other characters RFC 5424 doesn't allow, replaced with `_`
- Event names, event data keys and `send_log` could previously add or alter fields, such as a second structured data element
- An HTTP redirect from an OTLP collector is now an error instead of being followed, since the token and headers would be sent on to the new address. Configure the final address directly

## ✨ Enhancements

- Syslog over TLS can use a private certificate authority, and a client certificate for mutual TLS
- A Home Assistant repair issue is raised when an OTLP token is sent over plain HTTP
- Records added with `send_log` by a user carry that user's id as `user.id`
- `last_log` masks the value of every configured header, not only `Authorization`

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Syslog over TCP kept every record in memory, without limit, while the server couldn't be reached. Waiting records are now capped at 10,000 for both Syslog and OTLP, dropping the oldest
- A line within a Syslog message or stack trace that started with `<` could be read as a new record by receivers that split on newlines. Such lines are now indented by a space
- The whole error response of an OTLP collector was kept as a sensor attribute, and so recorded. It is now cut to 200 characters, as it already was in the log
- A failure to format an event wrote all of the event's data to the Home Assistant log, now only the event type

## 📝 Other changes

### Internal

- `SECURITY.md` added, with how to report a vulnerability, what the integration trusts, and known limitations
- Releases are published by a new *Publish Release* workflow, run on a draft release, which attaches the zip with a SHA-256 checksum and a build provenance attestation before publishing
- The tests of a pull request run with a read-only token, and pull requests no longer deploy the documentation or badges
- All GitHub Actions are pinned to a commit, and Bandit and zizmor run in CI
- The page view script on the documentation site is pinned to a version, with a subresource integrity hash
- The example Docker Compose files mount the Docker socket read-only and keep the Vector API to the local host

# 2.11.1

## ✨ Enhancements

- Strict RFC 5424 Syslog mode now defaults to SD-ID `homeassistant@67614`, using the IANA Private Enterprise Number assigned to Rhizomatics, instead of the RFC 5612 documentation number 32473
- Enter 32473 as the enterprise number to keep the previous SD-ID, e.g. for testing

# 2.11.0

## ✨ Enhancements

- Optional strict RFC 5424 mode for Syslog, for receivers such as Grafana Alloy that check messages closely
- Structured data uses Home Assistant names (`name`, `source`, `exception`, `event_type` and so on) and event data keys are shortened to fit the 32-character limit, e.g. `new.attr.friendly_name`
- `MSGID` is cut to 32 characters
- The SD-ID is `homeassistant@<number>`, using an IANA Private Enterprise Number if one is entered, otherwise the RFC 5612 documentation number 32473
- Off by default, so existing Syslog output, with its OTEL names, is unchanged

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Syslog messages for Home Assistant events other than `system_log_event` had an unquoted `eventName`, which strict RFC 5424 receivers rejected ([#113](https://github.com/rhizomatics/remote_logger/issues/113))
- Syslog `exception.stacktrace` values weren't escaped, so a stacktrace containing `"`, `\` or `]` broke the structured data ([#113](https://github.com/rhizomatics/remote_logger/issues/113))
- Log records from worker threads at the very end of Home Assistant shutdown no longer try to schedule a flush on the stopped event loop, which left a "coroutine was never awaited" warning and counted as a format error

## 📝 Other changes

### Internal

- mypy now runs in strict mode, meeting the Home Assistant Integration Quality Scale `strict-typing` rule

# 2.10.0

## 🚨 Breaking changes

- Support for Python 3.13, and versions of Home Assistant from 2026.4 and earlier no longer supported. They may continue to work, however there's no automated test assurance any longer, and newer features will start to be introduced
- Tested range is Home Assistant 2026.5.0 to 2026.10.x

## ✨ Enhancements

### Home Assistant Alignment

- Now declared as Bronze on the Home Assistant Integration Quality Scale, with a `quality_scale.yaml` tracking all the rules
- The `send_log`, `flush` and `last_log` actions are available before any entry has loaded, and give a clear error when no suitable entry is loaded
- Previously `send_log` and `flush` silently did nothing, and `last_log` returned an empty result
- Sensor unique IDs are now based on the config entry ID, so renaming an entry doesn't orphan its sensors
- Existing sensors are migrated automatically, keeping their entity IDs, history and customizations
- Integration category declared in the manifest, as `computers_network.monitoring`

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Re-authentication would have failed from Home Assistant 2026.12, leaving no way to replace an expired token
- Re-authentication could report success while the old token stayed in use
- Syslog over TLS and the configuration check no longer load the CA store in the event loop, which Home Assistant reported as a blocking call
- Authentication failures (401 or 403) now show "Authentication failed" on the configuration and re-authentication forms, rather than a connection failure
- Added the missing message for the mutually-exclusive state changes error in the options form

## 📚 Documentation

- Added removal instructions and an explanation of **Reconfigure** and **Configure** to the README and all its translations
- `quality_scale.yaml` added to document how this meets the Home Assistant standards

## 📝 Other changes

### Configuration UI

- Connection settings, such as host and token, have moved from **Configure** to **Reconfigure** in the integration entry's ⋮ menu. **Configure** now only covers the log level and event settings
- Existing settings are migrated automatically on upgrade
- Setup now checks the connection, so if the remote service is down when Home Assistant starts, the entry goes to "retrying setup" rather than loading and buffering. Logs from that period are not captured
- An OTLP 401 or 403 response starts re-authentication
- Each start or reload of an OTLP entry posts one validation log record to the remote service

### Internal

- CI tests against both the oldest and newest supported Home Assistant versions
- `ty` configuration aligned with other projects and skipped on pre-commit.ci, though it still runs in the local hook### Internalz

### Build Process Security

- Shared admin workflows pinned to a commit SHA
- `certifi` and `uv` updated in the development and CI environment, to pick up fixes for the eMudhra CA compromise

# 2.0.7

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- When you flip "Home Assistant state changes" on while the other, mutually-exclusive "state changes (without attributes)" toggle is already on, the flow correctly rejects it (state_changes_exclusive error) — but then re-renders the form using the old stored config values instead of what you just submitted. Now fixed, to use the newly supplied values.

## 📚 Documentation

- Additional Home Assistant events doc now gets a screenshot of what the full dialog looks like, and text improved.

# 2.0.6

## ✨ Enhancements

- OTLP validation now sends a single real log record, clearly marked as a configuration validation message, instead of an empty payload
- Some backends reject empty payloads (Loki with 422, Snowflake Observe with 400), and treating those codes as success also hid genuine problems such as a wrong encoding
- 400 and 422 responses are now reported as connection failures
- The message text is shown in the OTLP setup, options and reauth forms

# 2.0.5

## ✨ Enhancements

### Home Assistant Alignment

- Counters now persist properly as stats
- Diagnostic counter sensors (format errors, posting errors, events, postings) use the `total_increasing` state class instead of `measurement`
- **Warning**: existing long-term statistics for these sensors were recorded as measurements (mean/min/max). After upgrading, Home Assistant may report a state class change under *Developer Tools → Statistics*; use *Fix issue* there to delete or keep the old statistics

## 📝 Other changes

### Internal

- Added `ty` as additional type checker and tightened up some types
- Migrated `hass.data` calls to use `entry.runtime_data`

# 2.0.4

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Ruff checks extended, tightened, and fixes applied
- OTel formatting handles infinity correctly
- Dependencies updated

# 2.0.3

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Prevent `state_changed` event handling mutating event data and interfering with subsequent handlers

# 2.0.2

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Fixed test issues on CI, and improve HA async compatibility for log event handler

# 2.0.1

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Validation could fail with a 422 because of the empty payload when used with Loki, this status code is now taken to reflect remote service is available and authenticated

# 2.0.0

## ✨ Enhancements

### Root Log Handler

- New way to capture logs at any level
- `system_log_event` based logging is clean but limited to WARN and ERROR levels
  - System Log Event usage requires a YAML change to fire event
- Config now has a choice of using Python root logger
  - Configurable to a minimum log level (default `INFO` can be `DEBUG` if needed) which captures all logging
  - Reuses same logic as System Log to tie back exceptions to source code

# 1.6.0

## ✨ Enhancements

### py3.13 and py3.14

- Automated testing and linting is done for both Python 3.13 ( with the corresponding 2026.2 max Home Assistant version) and Python 3.14 with the latest Home Assistant public release

### Home Assistant Event improvements

- Corrected name of `repairs_issue_registry_updated`
- Improved description of core changes and serializing JSON
- Automation and script events generate title now only with entity_id for clarity and consistency with other events
- Tidied up ConfigFlow UI for Home Assistant standard events
- Defined message titles for all the device/entity/label/floor etc registries
- `system_log_event` is usually suppressed as an event name, since its noisy in a purely logging context. It can now optionally be emitted like any other event name, helpful if remote_logger being used more as a HA event store

# 1.5.1

## ✨ Enhancements

- For JSON, send integers as strings if they're not representable as signed 32 bit values, to meet limitations of JSON, and align with OTLP spec
- For JSON, suppress empty attributes and NaaN float values

# 1.5.0

- Timeout for remote posting now configurable, defaults to old hard-coded value 10
- OLTP JSON now in camel case, to suit strict interpretation by some log aggregators, and corrected handling of float/null values
- Added action to manually trigger log flush
- Added action to return the last posted submission to remote log service
- Fix switch from protobuf to JSON for an existing logger
